developer_request: Understand this small website/product prototype and tell me what should happen next.
known_facts: The README already identifies the product positioning, technology stack, routes, and important non-production boundaries.
The HANDOFF explicitly separates completed prototype surfaces from missing authentication, data, AI, permissions, and payment capabilities.
The HANDOFF gives a recommended integration order and a concrete first real end-to-end Definition of Done.
There is no need to read every component or generated output before identifying the next product/integration move.
expected_first_moves: Read README and HANDOFF as the initial project-state and transition entrypoints.
Inspect the manifest and only the implementation path relevant to the selected next integration step when needed.
Translate the handoff into one current high-value target rather than reconstructing the entire repository architecture.
Stop discovery when the current prototype boundary and one next implementation target are clear.
must_preserve: The explicit statement that the current login/prototype does not represent real authentication, family data, model calls, or active commercial terms.
The distinction between a deployable website and the unfinished real product loop.
must_not: Scan every component, route, generated static file, and document before naming the next useful step.
Manufacture a large project profile, architecture migration, or provider plan when the existing handoff already bounds the immediate decision.
Treat deployability of the static site as proof that the real family product is complete.
lessons: Small repositories need less discovery, not the same ceremony compressed into fewer files.
When README and handoff already establish current state and the next decision, deeper traversal should be triggered by a concrete implementation question.
